/-!
# Barnette's conjecture

Barnette's conjecture states that every cubic bipartite three-connected planar graph has a
Hamiltonian cycle. Equivalently, every bipartite polyhedral graph with three edges per vertex is
Hamiltonian.

Mathlib has no notion of planar graph. This file defines a planar embedding of a simple graph as a
drawing in the Euclidean plane without crossings: vertices go to distinct points and edges go to
arcs that meet only at common endpoints.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Barnette's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnette%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ba69] Barnette, D., *Conjecture 5*. In Tutte, W. T. (ed.), Recent Progress in Combinatorics,
  Academic Press (1969).
-/

blocks.code:
structure PlanarEmbedding (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The position of each vertex in the plane. -/
  vertex : V → ℝ²
  /-- The arc drawing each edge. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → I → ℝ²
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  continuous_arc (e : G.edgeSet) : Continuous (arc e)
  arc_injective (e : G.edgeSet) : Function.Injective (arc e)
  /-- The ends of the arc of an edge are the images of the endpoints of that edge. -/
  arc_zero_one (e : G.edgeSet) :
    ∃ u v, (e : Sym2 V) = s(u, v) ∧ arc e 0 = vertex u ∧ arc e 1 = vertex v
  /-- An arc meets the image of a vertex only if that vertex is an endpoint of its edge. -/
  mem_of_vertex_mem_range (e : G.edgeSet) (w : V) : vertex w ∈ Set.range (arc e) → w ∈ (e : Sym2 V)
  /-- Two different arcs meet only at images of vertices. -/
  mem_range_vertex_of_mem_inter (e e' : G.edgeSet) (he : e ≠ e') (p : ℝ²)
    (hp : p ∈ Set.range (arc e) ∩ Set.range (arc e')) : p ∈ Set.range vertex
blocks.docstring:
A planar embedding (a drawing without crossings) of a simple graph `G` in the Euclidean plane.

The vertices are sent to distinct points of the plane. Each edge is drawn as an arc, that is, a
continuous injective image of the unit interval `[0, 1]`, whose two ends are the images of the two
endpoints of the edge. No arc passes through the image of a vertex other than its own endpoints,
and two different arcs meet only at the images of vertices, which are then endpoints of both edges.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `Path`/`IsEmbedding` (used for Jordan curves in Wikipedia/InscribedSquare.lean) — `Path` is indexed by ordered endpoints, which does not fit `Sym2`-valued edges; no Kuratowski/Wagner (minor/subdivision) machinery exists in Mathlib to use as an alternative characterisation.
justification.name: BarnettesConjecture.PlanarEmbedding
justification.why_needed: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no notion of planar graph, planar embedding, graph minor or subdivision. This structure records a drawing of `G` in `ℝ²` (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), the repo's `ℝ²` notation): an injective vertex map, and for each edge (element of `G.edgeSet`) a continuous injective arc `I → ℝ²` whose ends are the images of the edge's two endpoints, such that an arc meets a vertex image only if that vertex is an endpoint of its edge, and two distinct arcs meet only at vertex images (hence only at common endpoints). This is exactly Diestel's definition of a plane graph, i.e. the Wikipedia article's 'can be embedded into the Euclidean plane without any crossings'.

def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (PlanarEmbedding G)
blocks.docstring: A simple graph is planar if it has a planar embedding in the Euclidean plane.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib (`rg -i planar|Kuratowski|Wagner|minor` in Mathlib/Combinatorics) and the repo: only unrelated matroid minors and a TODO mention in Coloring.lean; nothing usable.
justification.name: BarnettesConjecture.IsPlanar
justification.why_needed: Prop-valued planarity predicate: `Nonempty (PlanarEmbedding G)`. Accompanied by an API lemma `IsPlanar.mono` (subgraphs of planar graphs are planar) and a test `isPlanar_bot` (edgeless graph on a finite type is planar), both proved.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsPlanar.mono {G H : SimpleGraph V} (hHG : H ≤ G) (hG : IsPlanar G) : IsPlanar H := by
  obtain ⟨φ⟩ := hG
  have hincl : Function.Injective (Set.inclusion (edgeSet_mono hHG)) := Set.inclusion_injective _
  exact ⟨{
    vertex := φ.vertex
    arc e := φ.arc (Set.inclusion (edgeSet_mono hHG) e)
    vertex_injective := φ.vertex_injective
    continuous_arc e := φ.continuous_arc _
    arc_injective e := φ.arc_injective _
    arc_zero_one e := φ.arc_zero_one (Set.inclusion (edgeSet_mono hHG) e)
    mem_of_vertex_mem_range e w hw :=
      φ.mem_of_vertex_mem_range (Set.inclusion (edgeSet_mono hHG) e) w hw
    mem_range_vertex_of_mem_inter e e' he p hp :=
      φ.mem_range_vertex_of_mem_inter _ _ (hincl.ne he) p hp }⟩

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_bot [Fintype V] : IsPlanar (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) := by
  have hinj : Function.Injective
      (fun v : V => (WithLp.toLp 2 fun _ : Fin 2 => ((Fintype.equivFin V v : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℝ²)) := by
    intro v w hvw
    have := congrFun (congrArg (WithLp.ofLp (p := 2)) hvw) 0
    simpa using (Fintype.equivFin V).injective (Fin.ext (Nat.cast_injective this))
  have : IsEmpty (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet := by simp
  exact ⟨{
    vertex v := WithLp.toLp 2 fun _ : Fin 2 => ((Fintype.equivFin V v : ℕ) : ℝ)
    arc e := isEmptyElim e
    vertex_injective := hinj
    continuous_arc e := isEmptyElim e
    arc_injective e := isEmptyElim e
    arc_zero_one e := isEmptyElim e
    mem_of_vertex_mem_range e := isEmptyElim e
    mem_range_vertex_of_mem_inter e := isEmptyElim e }⟩

blocks.docstring:
**Barnette's conjecture.**

Every cubic bipartite three-connected planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.

Here a finite simple graph is *cubic* if every vertex has degree $3$, *bipartite* if its vertices
can be coloured with two colours so that no edge is monochromatic, *three-connected* if it has more
than $3$ vertices and stays connected after the removal of any set of at most $2$ vertices, and
*planar* if it can be drawn in the Euclidean plane without crossings. A planar three-connected
graph is also called *polyhedral*.

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop over finite simple graphs: hypotheses are 3-regular, bipartite (equivalently all faces even in a planar embedding), 3-vertex-connected (which for cubic graphs coincides with 3-edge-connected and forces ≥ 4 vertices, ruling out degenerate/empty cases) and planar (Mathlib has no planarity predicate, so an embedding/Kuratowski-style definition is needed); the conclusion is Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian`, whose ≥3-vertex convention is harmless here since the smallest instance is the cube graph on 8 vertices; the article's Kelmans and dual-tree-partition equivalents and the (now proved) Barnette–Goodey conjecture are not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same theorem shape over finite simple graphs: `IsRegularOfDegree 3` (cubic), Mathlib `IsBipartite`, the repo's `IsKConnected G 3` (3-vertex-connectivity: >3 vertices and connected after deleting <3 vertices; coincides with 3-edge-connectivity for cubic graphs, forces ≥4 vertices so `IsHamiltonian`'s `card ≠ 1` guard is inert), and a bespoke planarity predicate, concluding `G.IsHamiltonian`. They differ only in planarity. c01/c02/c03/c04/c06/c07 give direct topological crossing-free-drawing definitions matching the article's own definition ('embedded into the Euclidean plane without any crossings'); I verified each is neither too weak (vertices distinct, edges Jordan arcs between endpoint images, no vertex on an arc interior, distinct arcs meet only at vertex images hence common endpoints) nor too strong (any planar embedding yields the data). c05 uses straight-line drawings (correct only via Fáry's theorem) and c08 uses a rotation system with Euler's formula (equivalent to planarity only for connected graphs, as its own docstring admits), so both are less faithful as definitions of 'planar' even though correct under the hypotheses. Among the topological ones c07 is the cleanest: Mathlib idioms (`I`, `ℝ²`), well-named fields with docstrings, a general `isPlanar_bot` test and an `IsPlanar.mono` API lemma, full module/theorem docstrings with references. Shipped verbatim; compiles with only the `sorry` warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Barnette's conjecture

Barnette's conjecture states that every cubic bipartite three-connected planar graph has a
Hamiltonian cycle. Equivalently, every bipartite polyhedral graph with three edges per vertex is
Hamiltonian.

Mathlib has no notion of planar graph. This file defines a planar embedding of a simple graph as a
drawing in the Euclidean plane without crossings: vertices go to distinct points and edges go to
arcs that meet only at common endpoints.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Barnette's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnette%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ba69] Barnette, D., *Conjecture 5*. In Tutte, W. T. (ed.), Recent Progress in Combinatorics,
  Academic Press (1969).
-/

open SimpleGraph
open scoped EuclideanGeometry unitInterval

namespace BarnettesConjecture

variable {V : Type*}

/--
A planar embedding (a drawing without crossings) of a simple graph `G` in the Euclidean plane.

The vertices are sent to distinct points of the plane. Each edge is drawn as an arc, that is, a
continuous injective image of the unit interval `[0, 1]`, whose two ends are the images of the two
endpoints of the edge. No arc passes through the image of a vertex other than its own endpoints,
and two different arcs meet only at the images of vertices, which are then endpoints of both edges.
-/
structure PlanarEmbedding (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The position of each vertex in the plane. -/
  vertex : V → ℝ²
  /-- The arc drawing each edge. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → I → ℝ²
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  continuous_arc (e : G.edgeSet) : Continuous (arc e)
  arc_injective (e : G.edgeSet) : Function.Injective (arc e)
  /-- The ends of the arc of an edge are the images of the endpoints of that edge. -/
  arc_zero_one (e : G.edgeSet) :
    ∃ u v, (e : Sym2 V) = s(u, v) ∧ arc e 0 = vertex u ∧ arc e 1 = vertex v
  /-- An arc meets the image of a vertex only if that vertex is an endpoint of its edge. -/
  mem_of_vertex_mem_range (e : G.edgeSet) (w : V) : vertex w ∈ Set.range (arc e) → w ∈ (e : Sym2 V)
  /-- Two different arcs meet only at images of vertices. -/
  mem_range_vertex_of_mem_inter (e e' : G.edgeSet) (he : e ≠ e') (p : ℝ²)
    (hp : p ∈ Set.range (arc e) ∩ Set.range (arc e')) : p ∈ Set.range vertex

/-- A simple graph is planar if it has a planar embedding in the Euclidean plane. -/
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (PlanarEmbedding G)

/-- A subgraph of a planar graph is planar: keep the drawing and forget the missing edges. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsPlanar.mono {G H : SimpleGraph V} (hHG : H ≤ G) (hG : IsPlanar G) : IsPlanar H := by
  obtain ⟨φ⟩ := hG
  have hincl : Function.Injective (Set.inclusion (edgeSet_mono hHG)) := Set.inclusion_injective _
  exact ⟨{
    vertex := φ.vertex
    arc e := φ.arc (Set.inclusion (edgeSet_mono hHG) e)
    vertex_injective := φ.vertex_injective
    continuous_arc e := φ.continuous_arc _
    arc_injective e := φ.arc_injective _
    arc_zero_one e := φ.arc_zero_one (Set.inclusion (edgeSet_mono hHG) e)
    mem_of_vertex_mem_range e w hw :=
      φ.mem_of_vertex_mem_range (Set.inclusion (edgeSet_mono hHG) e) w hw
    mem_range_vertex_of_mem_inter e e' he p hp :=
      φ.mem_range_vertex_of_mem_inter _ _ (hincl.ne he) p hp }⟩

/-- The graph with no edges on a finite vertex type is planar. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_bot [Fintype V] : IsPlanar (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) := by
  have hinj : Function.Injective
      (fun v : V => (WithLp.toLp 2 fun _ : Fin 2 => ((Fintype.equivFin V v : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℝ²)) := by
    intro v w hvw
    have := congrFun (congrArg (WithLp.ofLp (p := 2)) hvw) 0
    simpa using (Fintype.equivFin V).injective (Fin.ext (Nat.cast_injective this))
  have : IsEmpty (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet := by simp
  exact ⟨{
    vertex v := WithLp.toLp 2 fun _ : Fin 2 => ((Fintype.equivFin V v : ℕ) : ℝ)
    arc e := isEmptyElim e
    vertex_injective := hinj
    continuous_arc e := isEmptyElim e
    arc_injective e := isEmptyElim e
    arc_zero_one e := isEmptyElim e
    mem_of_vertex_mem_range e := isEmptyElim e
    mem_range_vertex_of_mem_inter e := isEmptyElim e }⟩

variable [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]

/--
**Barnette's conjecture.**

Every cubic bipartite three-connected planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.

Here a finite simple graph is *cubic* if every vertex has degree $3$, *bipartite* if its vertices
can be coloured with two colours so that no edge is monochromatic, *three-connected* if it has more
than $3$ vertices and stays connected after the removal of any set of at most $2$ vertices, and
*planar* if it can be drawn in the Euclidean plane without crossings. A planar three-connected
graph is also called *polyhedral*.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem barnettes_conjecture (hcubic : G.IsRegularOfDegree 3) (hbip : G.IsBipartite)
    (hconn : IsKConnected G 3) (hplanar : IsPlanar G) : G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

end BarnettesConjecture

items: Planarity is modelled topologically (existence of a crossing-free drawing in ℝ² with Jordan arcs), the article's own definition, rather than via Kuratowski/Wagner obstructions, which would require additional undefined notions (subdivision/minor). A reviewer should check the embedding conditions: vertex map injective; each arc continuous and injective on [0,1] with ends at the two endpoint images; an arc contains a vertex image only for its own endpoints; distinct arcs intersect only in vertex images (hence in common endpoints).

Three-connectedness uses the repo's `SimpleGraph.IsKConnected G 3` (vertex connectivity): `3 < Fintype.card V` and `G - S` connected for every vertex set `S` with `|S| < 3`. This is the standard definition (Diestel) and matches the article's 'polyhedral = planar and 3-vertex-connected'; it also excludes degenerate graphs (K4 is non-bipartite, so the smallest instance is the cube).
Bipartite is Mathlib's `IsBipartite` (2-colourable), rather than the article's equivalent 'all faces even' formulation, which would need a notion of faces.
Cubic is `IsRegularOfDegree 3`; the graph is a finite simple graph (`SimpleGraph V`, `[Fintype V]`), as intended by the source (polyhedral graphs are simple).
The conclusion is Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian` (`card V ≠ 1 → ∃ Hamiltonian cycle`); the guard never triggers since 3-connectivity forces `card V > 3`.

The bespoke definitions are placed inside the problem file (namespace `BarnettesConjecture`) because the task restricts output to one file; in the repository proper they would belong in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/`. No proof that the cube graph satisfies the hypotheses is included (an explicit planar drawing proof would exceed the repository's proof-length guidance).

references.title: A computer-assisted proof of the Barnette-Goodey Conjecture: not only fullerene graphs are hamiltonian

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; no omissions. Ambiguity: 'three-connected' could mean vertex- or edge-connectivity, but these coincide for cubic graphs, and the article explicitly reads it as 3-vertex-connected (polyhedral); the repo's `IsKConnected` matches. Planarity has no Mathlib primitive, so the bespoke `PlanarEmbedding`/`IsPlanar` (topological drawing in ℝ² with Jordan arcs) is defined in the problem file; in the repository proper it would more naturally live in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/. The Kelmans / dual tree-partition equivalents and the (proved) Barnette–Goodey conjecture are not posed by the list entry and were not stated. All candidates compiled and every candidate's theorem was faithful modulo the planarity-definition quality noted above; none were rejected for unfaithfulness.
